OPERATIONAL ASSAY

Oxalate-extracted Fe(II) ferrozine assay in Ax17 ferrihydrite cultures

AssayMech:ax17-extracted-feii-ferrozine

Biotransformation

Measure extraction-defined Fe(II) during laboratory growth of D. ferrireducens Ax17 with synthetic two-line ferrihydrite, using ferrozine spectrophotometry after oxalate dissolution.

Download source YAML · View source at this revision

Scoped operational assay. Consult the sourced method, controls and limitations; missing protocol details remain explicit research gaps.

Record evidence

Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxide reduction by the thermophilic iron-reducing bacterium Desulfovulcanus ferrireducens — Primary methods measure Fe(II) with ferrozine after oxalate dissolution, including unfiltered and pre-dissolution-filtered fractions and uninoculated controls.

Source reference · html:#s2 · Source licence: CC-BY-4.0

Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxide reduction by the thermophilic iron-reducing bacterium Desulfovulcanus ferrireducens — The results report extracted Fe(II) in millimolar units; this is not a direct mineral identification.

Source reference · html:#s3 · Source licence: CC-BY-4.0

Interpretation and limitations
Oxalate extraction measures an operational Fe(II) pool; the unfiltered preparation is not a dissolved-iron measurement.
Ferrozine Fe(II) alone cannot identify magnetite or another mineral phase; the paper uses separate complementary mineral analyses.
Added FeCl2 and cysteine create a background requiring the matched abiotic controls.
The iron and ferrihydrite links describe the same experiment and do not constitute independent replication.
The Methods specifies 0.22 micrometre filtration, whereas the Results uses 0.2 micrometre wording; this record preserves the Methods value without inferring equivalence.
